structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment, Debt instruments, Rescheduling of payments due in current reporting period, on principal (memo item: o/w exceptional financing)
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct Investment represents cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Ownership of 10 percent or more of the voting power is evidence of a direct investment relationship. Debt instruments are financial instruments that require the payment of principal and/or interest at some point(s) in the future. Debt instruments consist of SDRs, currency and deposits, debt securities, loans, insurance technical reserves, pension and related entitlements, provision for calls under standardized guarantees, and other accounts receivable/payable. Rescheduling of payments due in current reporting period, on principal (memo item: o/w exceptional financing)

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Employee stock options, Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial instruments granted to employees as part of their compensation package, giving them the right to buy company stock at a predetermined price. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives, Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Financial instruments whose value is derived from the performance of underlying assets, indexes, or interest rates. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) and employee stock options, Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Negotiable financial instruments and employee stock options that are linked to other specific financial instruments, indicators, or commodities. Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Financial derivatives excluding those held as reserves and employee stock options. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Forward type, Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Forward type. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) options, Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Options contracts that are financial derivatives excluding those held as reserves. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Accumulation of arrears: total (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. The total sum of all overdue payments including principal, interest, and penalty interest, specifically highlighted when part of unique financing solutions. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) and employee stock options, Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6), Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Negotiable financial instruments and employee stock options that are linked to other specific financial instruments, indicators, or commodities. Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Financial derivatives excluding those held as reserves and employee stock options. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial derivatives (other than reserves) and employee stock options, Non financial corporations, households and NPISH, Net marked to market value
structure:Code.common:Description: Negotiable financial instruments and employee stock options that are linked to other specific financial instruments, indicators, or commodities. Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Financial derivatives excluding those held as reserves and employee stock options. Includes non-financial corporations, households, and non-profit institutions serving households. Net marked to market value

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Accumulation of arrears on principal (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. The total amount of principal payments that have fallen due but remain unpaid, separately recorded in the context of unusual financial arrangements. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Accumulation of arrears on penalty interest (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. The accumulation of overdue payments specifically on penalty interest charges, distinguished when associated with exceptional financing conditions. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Accumulation of arrears on original interest/coupon (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. The build-up of overdue payments on the initially agreed interest or coupon payments, noted separately when related to extraordinary financing measures. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment, Debt securities, Accumulation of arrears: total (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. The total sum of all overdue payments including principal, interest, and penalty interest, specifically highlighted when part of unique financing solutions. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment, Debt securities, Accumulation of arrears on principal (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. The total amount of principal payments that have fallen due but remain unpaid, separately recorded in the context of unusual financial arrangements. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment, Debt securities, Accumulation of arrears on original interest/coupon (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. The build-up of overdue payments on the initially agreed interest or coupon payments, noted separately when related to extraordinary financing measures. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment, Debt securities, Accumulation of arrears on penalty interest (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Sectors other than deposit-taking corporations and general government (Other Sectors - BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. The accumulation of overdue payments specifically on penalty interest charges, distinguished when associated with exceptional financing conditions. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment, Debt securities, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment, Debt securities, Long-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in more than one year, or has no stated maturity (referred to as long-term maturity)

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Debt instruments other than insurance, pension, and standardised schemes, Investment income, interest income
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Debt instruments other than insurance, pension, and standardised schemes. The cost of borrowing money, expressed as a percentage of the amount borrowed, paid by the borrower to the lender for the use of the lender's money.

structure:Codelist.common:Name: Country
structure:Codelist.common:Description: This codelist identifies the geographical, economic, or aggregate entities for which statistical data is collected and shared. It includes countries, territories (not necessarily recognized as states under international law), economic entities, and UN and IMF country groups used for statistical calculations.

structure:Code.common:Description: This is a country grouping established by the World Bank's classification of countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations. The list consists of (i) countries with high levels of institutional and social fragility and (ii) countries affected by violent conflict, using indicators and thresholds assessed by the World Bank. It is updated annually and available publicly. Under the new IMF strategy for Fragile and Conflicted States (FCS), the Fund has adopted the methodology, thresholds, and criteria of the World Bank's Fragility and Conflict Situations for the IMF Fragile and Conflicted States. This is explained in the FCS Strategy Board paper: The IMF Strategy for Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (March 14, 2022, p. 21-22).

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs): allocations, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. SDR allocations are reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and allocated to its member countries to supplement existing reserve assets. Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) are international reserve assets that the IMF allocates to its members as a form of supplementary liquidity. These allocations are based on each member country's IMF quota and are intended to provide additional liquidity and support to the global financial system. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Secondary income
structure:Code.common:Description: Secondary incomes are incomes arising from the distribution of income between institutional units via current transfers. In the context of the external accounts, this account records current transfers between residents and non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other short-term foreign currency liabilities to nonresidents: reserve-related (RRL) to nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Short-term foreign currency liabilities to nonresidents that are classified as reserve-related liabilities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Portfolio investment
structure:Code.common:Description: Portfolio investment reflects cross-border transactions and positions involving debt or equity securities, other than those included in direct investment or reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investor in direct invesment enterprises, Equity and investment fund shares
structure:Code.common:Description: An investor that makes direct investment in enterprises, having control or significant influence. Ownership interest in companies (equity) and shares in investment funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets in SDR basket
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserve assets that are part of the Special Drawing Rights (SDR) basket.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment, Investment fund shares/units
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct Investment represents cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Ownership of 10 percent or more of the voting power is evidence of a direct investment relationship. Shares or units in a fund that pools investor money to purchase securities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment enterprises in direct investor, Equity and investment fund shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Enterprises in which direct investment is made by the investor. Ownership interest in companies (equity) and shares in investment funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Debt instruments, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Financial instruments that require the payment of principal and/or interest at some point(s) in the future, including SDRs, currency and deposits, debt securities, loans, insurance technical reserves, and other accounts receivable/payable. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Loans, credit, and loans with the IMF (other than reserves), General government, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Financial instruments including loans, credit, and loans with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), excluding those held as reserves. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment between fellow enterprises if ultimate controlling parent is unknown, Equity and investment fund shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Investment between enterprises controlled by the same parent entity, where the status of the parent entity's residency is unknown. Ownership interest in companies (equity) and shares in investment funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment between fellow enterprises if ultimate controlling parent is resident, Equity and investment fund shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Investment between enterprises controlled by the same parent entity, where the parent entity is a resident of the country. Ownership interest in companies (equity) and shares in investment funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment between fellow enterprises if ultimate controlling parent is nonresident, Equity and investment fund shares
structure:Code.common:Description: Investment between enterprises controlled by the same parent entity, where the parent entity is not a resident of the country. Ownership interest in companies (equity) and shares in investment funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Credit and loans from the IMF: reserve-related liabilities (RRL) to nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserve-related liabilities owed to nonresidents arising from credit and loans provided by the IMF.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Other debt instruments, Adjusted using IMF accounting records

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Long-term

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions (net): nonproduced assets

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment, Primary income
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct Investment represents cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. structure:Code.common:Name: Financial account balance (assets less liabilities)

In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. The monetary authority of a country responsible for issuing currency and regulating the banking system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other sectors: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Miscellaneous or residual sectors not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. The monetary authority of a country responsible for issuing currency and regulating the banking system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other financial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations not classified under other specific financial sub-sectors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other sectors: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Miscellaneous or residual sectors not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other financial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations not classified under other specific financial sub-sectors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on monetary authorities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on monetary authorities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on other entities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on other entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Reserve position in the IMF
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve position in the IMF is the sum of a member’s reserve tranche position and any indebtedness of the IMF in the General Resources Account (GRA) that is readily available to the member to meet balance of payments financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total liabilities, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of all financial obligations owed by an entity to other entities. These obligations represent claims held by others against the entity and may include loans, debt securities, accounts payable, and other forms of debt. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total assets, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Total assets This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6), Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6), Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Description: This is a country grouping established by the World Bank's classification of countries in fragile and conflict-affected situations. The list consists of (i) countries with high levels of institutional and social fragility and (ii) countries affected by violent conflict, using indicators and thresholds assessed by the World Bank. It is updated annually and available publicly. Under the new IMF strategy for Fragile and Conflicted States (FCS), the Fund has adopted the methodology, thresholds, and criteria of the World Bank's Fragility and Conflict Situations for the IMF Fragile and Conflicted States. This is explained in the FCS Strategy Board paper: The IMF Strategy for Fragile and Conflict-Affected States (March 14, 2022, p. 21-22).

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

The term current external balance is used in the national accounts and is expressed from the perspective of the non-resident units, and therefore with the opposite sign.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment, Investment fund shares/units, Money market funds

Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Ownership interest in companies (equity) and shares in investment funds.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Debt securities, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Credit and loans with the IMF: other than reserves, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Credit and loans provided by the IMF that are not related to reserve assets. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Debt securities, Long-term

Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in more than one year, or has no stated maturity (referred to as long-term maturity)

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Accumulation of arrears: total (memo item: o/w exceptional financing), Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Reserve position in the IMF, Central bank

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Reserve position in the IMF

Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve position in the IMF is the sum of a member’s reserve tranche position and any indebtedness of the IMF in the General Resources Account (GRA) that is readily available to the member to meet balance of payments financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Description: Secondary incomes are incomes arising from the distribution of income between institutional units via current transfers. In the context of the external accounts, this account records current transfers between residents and non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs): allocations, Adjusted using IMF accounting records

SDR allocations are reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and allocated to its member countries to supplement existing reserve assets. Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) are international reserve assets that the IMF allocates to its members as a form of supplementary liquidity. These allocations are based on each member country's IMF quota and are intended to provide additional liquidity and support to the global financial system. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Direct investment, Debt instruments, Rescheduling of payments due in current reporting period, on principal (memo item: o/w exceptional financing)
structure:Code.common:Description: Direct Investment represents cross-border investment associated with a resident in one economy having control or a significant degree of influence on the management of an enterprise that is resident in another economy. Debt instruments are financial instruments that require the payment of principal and/or interest at some point(s) in the future. structure:Code.common:Name: Secondary income
structure:Code.common:Description: Secondary incomes are incomes arising from the distribution of income between institutional units via current transfers. In the context of the external accounts, this account records current transfers between residents and non-residents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Net lending (+) / net borrowing (-)
structure:Code.common:Description: Net lending is the difference between changes in net worth due to saving and capital transfers and net acquisitions of non-financial assets (acquisitions less disposals of non-financial assets, less depreciation). If the amount is negative, it represents net borrowing. In the external accounts, it represents the sum of the balances on the current and capital accounts. This is conceptually equal to the net balance of the financial account. If the balance is positive, it is called net lending, implying that in net terms, the economy supplies funds to the rest of the world. If the balance is negative, it is called net borrowing, implying that in net terms, the economy receives funds from the rest of the world.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Monetary gold: gold bullion

Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Gold in the form of bars or ingots held as a reserve asset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Unallocated gold accounts
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Unallocated gold accounts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on monetary authorities, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on monetary authorities. Central bank

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on other entities, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on other entities. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund and allocated to its members to supplement existing reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Nonmonetary gold
structure:Code.common:Description: Nonmonetary gold

structure:Code.common:Name: Total financial assets/liabilities, Investment income on other investment income
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of financial assets and liabilities. Investment income

structure:Code.common:Name: Other primary income
structure:Code.common:Description: Primary incomes are incomes earned by institutional units as a consequence of their involvement in processes of production or ownership of assets that may be needed for purposes of production.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income on rent
structure:Code.common:Description: Rent

structure:Code.common:Name: Acquisitions nonproduced nonfinancial assets
structure:Code.common:Description: Acquisitions nonproduced nonfinancial assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: All modes of transport; other than passenger and freight; including postal and courier services
structure:Code.common:Description: Transportation services excluding the transport of passengers, goods, and also including postal and courier activities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Transport, Passenger, Of which: Payable by Border, Seasonal, and Other S-T Workers
structure:Code.common:Description: Transport, Passenger, Of which: Payable by Border, Seasonal, and Other S-T Workers

structure:Code.common:Name: Travel services, Both Business and Personal Travel, Other Services
structure:Code.common:Description: Travel services, Both Business and Personal Travel, Other Services.

structure:Code.common:Name: Other investment, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)
structure:Code.common:Description: Other investment represents a residual investment category that includes positions and transactions other than those included in direct investment, portfolio investment, financial derivatives and employee stock options, and reserve assets. Reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund and allocated to its members to supplement existing reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve assets created by the International Monetary Fund and allocated to its members to supplement existing reserve assets.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Monetary gold: gold bullion
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Gold in the form of bars or ingots held as a reserve asset.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Monetary gold: of which gold under swap for cash collateral
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Portion of monetary gold that is held under swap agreements for cash collateral.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Unallocated gold accounts
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Unallocated gold accounts.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Financial derivatives
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Negotiable financial instruments linked to another specific financial instrument, indicator, or commodity, through which specific risks (e.g., interest rate risk, foreign exchange risk, equity and commodity price risk, credit risk) can be traded in their own right in financial markets. Financial instruments whose value is derived from the performance of underlying assets, indexes, or interest rates.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Debt securities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Tradable financial instruments representing a debt, such as bonds and notes.

structure:Code.common:Name: Investment income on other investment income
structure:Code.common:Description: Investment income

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserves and Related items
structure:Code.common:Description: Reserves and Related items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial account balance, excluding reserves and related items
structure:Code.common:Description: Financial account balance, excluding reserves and related items.

structure:Code.common:Name: Financial account balance (assets less liabilities), Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: The financial account balance reflects the difference in transactions in financial assets and liabilities in the accounting period. In the external accounts, only transactions between residents and non-residents are included. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. The monetary authority of a country responsible for issuing currency and regulating the banking system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other sectors: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Miscellaneous or residual sectors not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Central bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. The monetary authority of a country responsible for issuing currency and regulating the banking system.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents total, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: The aggregate notional value of all foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other financial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations not classified under other specific financial sub-sectors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, General government
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Central, state, and local governments, including their agencies and departments.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other sectors: Other
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Miscellaneous or residual sectors not classified elsewhere.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Other financial corporations
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations not classified under other specific financial sub-sectors.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Foreign currency derivatives by sector notional value of contracts with nonresidents, Deposit taking corporations, except the Central Bank
structure:Code.common:Description: The total notional value of foreign currency derivative contracts with nonresidents, categorized by sector. Financial corporations accepting deposits, except for the central bank.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on monetary authorities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on monetary authorities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Currency and deposits, Claims on other entities
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Monetary assets held in the form of currency or in deposit accounts with financial institutions, claims on other entities.

structure:Code.common:Name: Reserve assets, Reserve position in the IMF
structure:Code.common:Description: External assets that are readily available to and controlled by monetary authorities for meeting balance of payments financing needs, for intervention in exchange markets to affect the currency exchange rate, and for other related purposes (such as maintaining confidence in the currency and the economy, and serving as a basis for foreign borrowing). Reserve assets must be denominated and settled in foreign currency. Reserve position in the IMF is the sum of a member’s reserve tranche position and any indebtedness of the IMF in the General Resources Account (GRA) that is readily available to the member to meet balance of payments financing needs.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total liabilities, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: The total value of all financial obligations owed by an entity to other entities. These obligations represent claims held by others against the entity and may include loans, debt securities, accounts payable, and other forms of debt. This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Total assets, Adjusted using IMF accounting records
structure:Code.common:Description: Total assets This indicator has been adjusted using IMF accounting records received from the IMF Finance Department.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6), Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt liabilities to nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Liabilities owed to nonresidents in the form of debt. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6)
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Other Sectors (BPM6), Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Sectors excluding deposit-taking corporations and general government. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents.

structure:Code.common:Name: Debt claims on nonresidents, Short-term
structure:Code.common:Description: Claims for debt owed by nonresidents. Original contract stipulates that payment is due in one year or less or payable on demand (referred to as short-term maturity).
